title: Intonation: Teschemacher's quarter tones and Pee Wee
summary: They argue that Tesh's out-of-tune effects were deliberate, comparing classical just intonation and Pee Wee Russell.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: there is a suggestion in many of the earlier records that some of the bands were awfully sloppy on intonation for example now even when we get ten years later into the Chicagoan period some of those fellas must have known that their intonation was imperfect was this for an effect or was this matter ignored or how do you account for intonation well I think
you're not talking about Tesh for instance
well I think Tesh was quite consciously doing it when he'd get a quarter tone off
so this was the proper intonation for what he wanted to do
yeah I'd say he was just about as conscious as I was Hindemith although he couldn't have explained it quite so well but I think he was right on the button on what he wanted

to play the drummers you don't talk about are the drummers but when you get up to a trumpet player who would use an unusual slur which might very easily involve unexplained passing notes or a brashness that was really outside the scope of prior trumpet he knew what he was doing and he was trying to say something new and more

yes some people said that Tesh's clarinet was out of tune for instance well I had it for a while it's a buffet and it isn't it was a perfectly beautiful instrument and I lent it to somebody unfortunately he was quite conscious of everything he was doing also I think that some of them had this diatonic scale in mind in the way that some classical musicians do in the sense that you could play a trombone or a violin and of course hit the hit the right note rather than the tempered note oh yes you see where I mean an F
and it would be something of a surprise because you weren't yeah

where F flat would be considerably lower than E natural for example and I think they'd be quite conscious of that classical clarinets do it all the time Jo Stafford sings that way she sounds out of tune

half the time because she's reading that could be sure what was happening or for that matter might not even distinguish from it I think there are too few examples for us to dwell on that subject in fact I'm frightened by it because I know how imperfect my ear is and how exact an instrument could show those differences

Pee Wee in ensemble work is a wonderful example of that when Pee Wee will play a chorus that has many atonalities let's say in it then you listen to him in the ensemble it'll be clean as a whistle and right on the button and those high notes are beautiful he'd never do it then he'd only do it when he's expressing himself on some in a way exactly the way he wanted to Pee Wee has never played anything he didn't intend to play

I'm sure that we've begun to get into a marsh of questions here beyond the scope of common understanding and when you talk about the musician being a critic this is only where the musician can tread with safety is in these matters of the tempered scale and understanding of these slight shadings
